rules.rationale: A declared requirement points down or stays in its layer, never up: the foundation, the transport, the collectors, their entries and the collection are the read side, and the contract, the model, its barrier, the evaluation, the report and the core are the decision side above it.

A component is used only through the names that it lists in public. A crate root is the one public path of each name that it publishes: another crate uses such a name through the root, and a deeper path of it is no public path (AD-608). A method call reaches the module of its impl block and passes through the publication of its type (AD-604).
The symbol table reads shared module data, not the survey (AD-389).
Expression text is below the survey (AD-389).
Expression text is below the symbol table (AD-389).
Shared module data is below the survey (AD-389).
Shared module data is below the symbol table (AD-389).
Shared module data does not write expression text (AD-389).
The tree view is below the survey (AD-389).
The tree view is below the symbol table (AD-389).
The tree view does not write expression text (AD-389).
The parse is below the survey (AD-389).
The parse is below the symbol table (AD-389).
The parse does not write expression text (AD-389).
A module that no component owns escapes every rule below.
A component uses another component only where requires says so; absence forbids. This is the crate direction of AD-327 and the module direction of each collector.
Components stay layered: facts, wire and snapshot are the base, and the flow of a collector is above its parts.
Modules use each other in one direction, so a module is read, tested and moved after the modules it uses; the component rule cannot see a cycle inside one component.
Only a collector parses source with Tree-sitter; no library crate does.
Only the TypeScript collector loads the TypeScript grammar.
Only the Rust collector parses Rust source with syn.
Only a grammar crate links a C parser to a Tree-sitter language; a collector gets the language from the grammar crate.
Only the parse modules of the Python collector use the Python parser, so a parser update cannot reach discovery, naming or records.

Only the parse modules, the tree readers of the survey, the CPython view of the tree, the expression text and the definition table of the Python collector read the tree of the Python parser; discovery, naming and the entry read owned values.
Only the Python collector reads pyproject.toml and only archkeel-collect reads archkeel.toml (AD-406); the core side (model, eval, report, core) reads no TOML.
Only the lexical modules of the Rust collector read token spans, next to syn.
Only the survey module and the CPython view, the string check and the definition table of the Python collector read the text ranges of the Python parser (AD-377).
Only a grammar crate compiles a vendored C parser.
Only the store and the wire decompress a reply or a request.
Only the facts crate and the crates of the core frame derive a JSON schema: the facts (AD-345) and the frame of the core (AD-596).
Only the contract parser checks a Python identifier with the XID tables.
These crates compute source digests, or the report's build-time script hashes; the model, evaluator and core copy digests and compute none.
These crates encode or decode typed values; the evaluator and the collectors that write through the facts crate do not.
These crates read or write JSON; the evaluator reads typed values only.
Only the Dart package survey reads YAML package metadata.
Each external crate has a stated home: an import of a crate that no rule names fails.
